# Vincent Runge

**Assistant Professor of Statistics** · Université d’Évry Paris-Saclay · LaMME (CNRS UMR 8071)

My research focuses on change-point detection and efficient algorithms for structured data. I work on dynamic programming and pruning methods, extensions to non-Euclidean spaces, and computational geometry for time-series analysis.

::: {.profile-links}
[GitHub](https://github.com/vrunge) · [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=YzxaQlsAAAAJ&hl=fr) · [Email](mailto:vincent.runge@univ-evry.fr)
:::
:::
:::

## Current position

I have been an Assistant Professor in Statistics at Université d’Évry Paris-Saclay since September 2019. I am a member of the [LaMME laboratory](http://www.math-evry.cnrs.fr).

## Research interests

- Change-point detection, dynamic programming and functional pruning
- Methods for complex data in Hadamard and CAT spaces
- Computational geometry and time-series compression
- Constrained and convex optimization
- Topological Data Analysis

See the [research overview](research.qmd) and [publications](publications.qmd).

## Supporting Ukrainian Mathematics Students

Since 2022, I have dedicated a significant part of my time to supporting Ukrainian mathematics students in obtaining scholarships, in collaboration with the FMJH through the [FMJHcare program](https://www.fondation-hadamard.fr/fr/programmes/les-programmes-transverses/fmjh-care/) and the [FSMP](https://sciencesmaths-paris.fr). So far, we have helped about 40 students with different programs. I also advise them on finding internships, improving their CVs and motivation letters, and navigating the complex French higher-education system. 

<span class="danger-sign" aria-label="Announcement">🎺</span> The [UMD 2026 conference at IHP](https://ukrmathday2026.sciencesconf.org) and the [UMD 2025 day in Évry](https://indico.math.cnrs.fr/event/13784/) are examples of this ongoing effort. 

::: {.exhibition-highlight}
**Mathematics in Ukraine: continuing traditions**

As a side event of the UMD 2026 conference, I proposed and coordinated an exhibition created by my colleagues in Ukraine. It was displayed in the entrance hall of the **Henri Poincaré Institute** from May to October 2026.

The contributors are:

- **Iryna Banakh**, Institute for Applied Problems of Mechanics and Mathematics (Lviv), National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine.
- **Taras Banakh, Viktoriia Brydun, Olena Hryniv, Yaroslav Prytula, and Mykhailo Zarichnyi**, Ivan Franko National University of Lviv.

**Conception & Graphic Design:** [Wonjin Park](https://www.linkedin.com/in/wonjin-park-b800a1224/?locale=en)

The exhibition panels are available online in this [PDF file](FINAL%20version%20UKR.pdf). The Poincaré Institute can send the panels to other institutions in France or abroad upon request. 
:::


<span class="danger-sign" aria-label="Warning">⚠️</span> **Ukrainian students in mathematics are welcome to contact me for advice and support** (one easy task is to connect them with other Ukrainian students in a similar situation).

## Past responsibilities

- I headed the [Paris-Saclay M2 Data Science programme (M2 Data Science : Santé, Assurance, Finance)](https://www.universite-paris-saclay.fr/en/education/masters-degree/mathematics-and-applications/m2-data-science-health-insurance-and-finance) in 2022–2023 and co-directed it with [Agathe Guilloux](https://sites.google.com/view/agatheguilloux-personalwebsite/accueil) in 2020–2022. From 2023 to 2026, I continued to take an active part in the programme’s organization, particularly in student selection as well as in internship defense.
- I created and co-organized the [Math For Genomics seminar](https://mathforgenomics.github.io/).
